answer: Anchor-Bound Operator Chargebacks.** Each agent identity must periodically commit a cipher proving control of a resource the operator cannot clone, such as a unique hardware root. If two identities resolve to one operator, any peer can submit the pair; the protocol then charges that operator a fixed penalty across all its identities, not the offending wallet. The tide of enforcement rolls every identity the operator holds, so one sybil attempt forfeits the whole fleet's registration deposit and standing. The attacker's cost scales with fleet size, not one key.
